name: Juxtaposition of the Atrial Appendages

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Surgical Diagnostic Criteria for Juxtaposition of Atrial Appendages

criteria.description: Visualization of both atrial appendages positioned abnormally on the same side of the great arteries by echocardiography
Intraoperative confirmation of atrial appendage juxtaposition during cardiac surgery
Presence of associated congenital heart defects such as transposition of the great arteries or ventricular septal defect

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of echocardiographic visualization of juxtaposed atrial appendages plus either surgical confirmation or associated congenital cardiac anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often made during evaluation for complex congenital heart disease.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Juxtaposition of atrial appendages detected on imaging
searchTerms: abnormal position of atrial appendages on imaging
abnormal shape of atria on heart ultrasound

common.symptomName: Cyanosis due to associated transposition of the great arteries
searchTerms: bluish skin due to heart vessel transposition

common.symptomName: Heart murmur from associated septal defects
searchTerms: abnormal heart sounds due to septal defects
heart valve or septum related murmur
failure to gain weight as baby
abnormal heart rhythm due to atrial position
poor sucking or swallowing in neonates

occasional.symptomName: Mild hepatomegaly due to congestive heart failure
searchTerms: slightly enlarged liver from heart failure
mild liver swelling due to congestion

rare.symptomName: Stroke or embolic events related to atrial abnormalities
searchTerms: stroke caused by heart atrial problems

rare.symptomName: Severe congestive heart failure in infancy

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia in cyanotic patients
Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Cardiac MRI or CT confirming atrial appendage position
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly or pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; often sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Electrocardiogram showing arrhythmias or atrial enlargement

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated septal defect without atrial malposition

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
references: Anderson RH, et al. The anatomy of juxtaposition of the atrial appendages. Cardiol Young. 2010;20(1):1-8.
